regulator.title: Declaratory Ruling on Review of Upstream Ownership Transactions

pageFindings.finding: May17 ruling resolves the GIP project-interest and BlackRock upstream-manager petitions by finding no further PSL70 review required under the Wallkill presumption. It assumes future consummation; neither ruling date nor closed proceeding establishes transaction closing.

South Fork Wind, LLC is wholly owned by South Fork Wind Holdings, LLC. South Fork Class B Member, LLC owns the managing Class B interests in Holdings; Eversource Investment LLC and Orsted SF Class B Member, LLC each own50% in that Class B vehicle. Eversource TEI LLC separately holds passive Class A non-managing interests. North East Offshore, LLC is separately owned50/50 by Eversource Investment and Orsted DevCo, LLC and owns Revolution Wind. Footnote8 excludes Sunrise before closing.

The proposed buyer is GIP IV Whale Fund Holdings, L.P. and/or designated affiliates. The GP is Global Infrastructure GP IV L.P.; its general partner Global Infrastructure Investors IV, LLC is defined as GIP IV. GIM Participation Fund Holding LP owns that LLC. These are distinct legal persons and the short GIP IV definition is not authority to expand the legal buyer into an inferred flagship fund or BlackRock GIF IV.

Orsted SF Class B Member and Orsted DevCo are corporate subsidiaries of Orsted North America Inc., indirectly owned by Ørsted A/S. Ørsted's interests are unchanged by the GIP transaction. These are direct corporate project vehicles, not an undisclosed managed fund.

Additional intermediate companies and passive investors may be introduced; material control changes require amendments. At the ruling date no such passive arrangements had been reported. The exact designated closing affiliate and complete closing chain are not established by this conditional ruling.

The subsequent BlackRock acquisition transfers upstream manager/GP control and hence indirect control, not a second acquisition of the same project interest. Preserve the existing GIP period and do not infer a separate BlackRock project owner or deny the upstream ownership change.

The regulatory discussion explicitly distinguishes50% indirect Class B ownership at South Fork from retained passive Class A interests. Footnote17 describes50% indirect Revolution ownership; the projects are not the same legal entity. Remaining market-power and ratepayer analysis is not fund-identity evidence.
